idea.open_problems:
1.  How to guarantee that single-digit-NFE discrete diffusion remains reliable when simultaneously (i) the target device throttles clock or enters thermal-limiting states and (ii) user prompts create highly bursty, long-range dependencies that violate i.i.d. token-entropy assumptions.
2.  Even with mixed-precision, GEMM still dominates energy; however, on many NPUs the memory hierarchy (DMA traffic, SRAM row-buffer misses) burns a comparable or larger share.  No sampler today co-optimises arithmetic energy and memory-traffic energy under a global statistical error budget.
3.  Current per-span grouping is heuristic (conditional-entropy < τ).  We lack a principled way to decide (a) which spans to merge and (b) whether to reuse previously computed logits, in order to minimise expected energy given a forecast of future steps.
4.  Theoretical certification is limited to KL→ BLEU bounds.  Safety-critical code generation, for instance, needs guarantees on functional semantics (unit-test pass@k) while music tasks care about rhythmic structure.  A generic path from distributional divergence to task-specific structured metrics is missing.
5.  Compiler support for zero-skip / mixed-precision kernels exists in TVM-Relax, but real vendors (Apple ANE, MediaTek APU) expose only opaque NNAPI packs.  A vendor-independent IR that carries sampling-time decisions (Δt,b,jump_mask) down to binary blobs is not yet standardised.
idea.methods:
We propose CERBERUS-RELAX (Certified Energy & Reuse Based RELAXation), a three-pillar extension to ECO-RELAX.
Pillar-1  Memory-traffic aware PAC bound.
•  We extend the telescoping KL analysis with an additional error term due to feature-reuse quantisation.  Using matrix Bernstein inequality we show that if reused hidden states are refreshed whenever the cumulative reused-step variance exceeds σ²_max, then the incremental TV divergence grows ≤ ε_mem per refresh interval.  This allows dynamic scheduling of ‘refresh points’ that trade DMA energy against provable global divergence.
Pillar-2  Meta-planning via stochastic shortest path.
•  We cast the joint choice of (Δt_i, b_i, reuse_flag_i, span_merge_i) as a stochastic shortest-path (SSP) where edge cost is predicted energy (MAC + SRAM + DRAM) and edge risk is the certified incremental KL.  A lightweight value-iteration policy, pre-computed once per device class, outputs near-optimal action tables indexed by (token-entropy, predicted variance credit, temperature).
•  At run-time the sampler reads the current device thermal headroom H and scales the SSP cost vector, thus adapting to throttling without breaking certificates.
Pillar-3  Structured-metric calibration.
•  We derive a generic conversion from global KL to expected loss under any decomposable metric that can be expressed as a weighted sum of n-gram indicator functions (BLEU, Rouge-L), constraint violations (syntax parse errors) or rhythmic on-grid penalties.  The weights are estimated once from held-out data via importance weighting; Chebyshev concentration gives a PAC(δ) bound.
•  For code we additionally plug in a learned semantic embedding; we bound the probability of unit-test failure by the cosine margin between embeddings, thanks to recent robustness results for contrastive models.
Hardware stack.
•  We extend TVM-Relax with ‘CertOp’—an intrinsic that carries (<energy_coeffs>,<kl_credit>) metadata.  A new back-end pass lowers CertOp to NNAPI / CoreML custom ops and emits side-band JSON that the firmware can inspect to decide DVFS levels.

idea.open_problems:
1. Memory-traffic, thermal throttling and arithmetic precision interact in highly non-linear ways that the current matrix-Bernstein based bound cannot capture once we move to sub-4-bit or sparsity-pruned kernels.
2. Error budgets are allocated per sampling trajectory, yet many realistic applications (streaming translation, live coding) run continuous sessions where quality can be recovered later.  We lack a mechanism to redistribute the unused part of the statistical budget across utterances while still guaranteeing worst-case bounds.
3. The SSP planner in CERBERUS-RELAX is hand-derived and fixed per device-class; it cannot exploit on-line telemetry (DVFS state, cache-miss counters) nor adapt when the firmware is updated over time.
4. Structured-metric conversion still relies on loose Chebyshev concentration; for safety-critical code we would like step-wise semantic invariants rather than end-of-sequence bounds.
5. Vendor-neutral IR exists for Δt,b,jump_mask but does not yet encode the accompanying certificates, making downstream verification impossible once kernels are linked.
idea.methods:
We propose ALCHEMY-RELAX (Adaptive Learned Certifiable Hardware-Energy co-scheduling for Multimodal diffUsion) that extends CERBERUS in four directions.
M1. Hierarchical PAC-Bayesian envelope.
   • Replace the single Bernstein term with a two-level PAC-Bayesian bound that treats (i) low-precision arithmetic noise and (ii) sparse SRAM row conflicts as independent stochastic processes.  This yields tighter ≤ε_tot bounds even with INT2 and unstructured weight sparsity.
M2. Budget banking & rollover.
   • Introduce an online ‘credit ledger’: after each utterance we measure the realised divergence and credit the difference (ε_budget–ε_real) into a bank.  A martingale-based super-martingale argument guarantees that the cumulative divergence across an unlimited session stays ≤ε_global with probability 1–δ, while allowing later hard segments to draw on saved credit.
M3. Telemetry-driven safe RL scheduler.
   • Replace fixed SSP tables with a certifiably-safe Reinforcement-Learning agent trained with Constrained Policy Optimisation.  State = (token-entropy histogram, thermal headroom, LLC miss rate, ε_bank).  Action = (Δt, b, reuse_flag, span_merge).  A Lagrange multiplier keeps the learned policy inside the PAC envelope; proofs show monotone improvement over the hand-crafted baseline without certificate violation.
M4. Symbolic semantic guard.
   • For code generation we incorporate an on-the-fly static analyser that emits linear-time temporal logic (LTL) invariants for each partially generated AST.  Using results from probably-approximately-correct model checking, we translate incremental TV divergence into an upper bound on invariant-violation probability at every step, not just at the end.
M5. Certificate-carrying IR (ccIR).
   • We extend TVM-Relax/MLIR with a ‘ccIR’ section that serialises per-kernel (energy_coeff, kl_credit, invariant_guard) triplets.  Mobile firmware can therefore refuse to load a model if the binary was altered or the certificate is missing.
idea.experimental_setup:
Benchmarks: LONG-BENCH-v3 (adds 12-minute symphony, 16-file enterprise repo, 10k-token dialogue), plus a continuous-stream setting that runs 30-minute mixed tasks.
Devices: Snapdragon 8-Gen-3, Apple M3-Max, Dimensity 9300, Intel Meteor-Lake NPU, ESP32-S3 (micro-controller for extreme low-power test).
Baselines: ECO-RELAX, SKIP-RELAX, PTQD+DeepCache, BitsFusion-int2.
Metrics: (i) Quality & safety – BLEU, COMET, pass@k, rhythmic F-measure, per-step invariant-violation prob. (ii) Energy and memory traffic via on-chip counters. (iii) Certificate utilisation (ε_used / ε_budget). (iv) Session-level QoS under thermal shock profiles. (v) ccIR compile & verification latency.
Ablations: disable budget banking; RL→table lookup; remove symbolic guard; INT2→INT4; no sparsity.
idea.expected_result:
• INT2+25 % unstructured sparsity achieves further 1.4× energy cut vs CERBERUS while keeping ε_tot≤0.2 nats.
• Budget banking reduces worst-case BLEU drop by 35 % over 30-min sessions under bursty load.

• Step-wise invariant guard limits unit-test failure probability to ≤2 % at every generation step (down from 7 % end-only guarantee).
• ccIR adds <1 % binary size and <4 ms extra verification time on Android firmware.
idea.expected_conclusion: ALCHEMY-RELAX shows that discrete diffusion can be both ultra-low-energy (INT2+sparsity) and formally safe in continuous, real-world usage.  Hierarchical PAC-Bayesian envelopes, credit-rollover and safe RL planning cut energy another factor 1.4×–2× beyond the state-of-the-art, while the new certificate-carrying IR enables end-to-end verifiability from Python to firmware.  The framework bridges learning theory, symbolic verification and mobile systems, paving the way for trustworthy always-on generative AI on commodity edge devices.

evaluate.novelty_reason: Existing acceleration works for discrete diffusion (DNDM, Continuous-time CTMC, DeepCache, FasterDiffusion, ASE, AMED-Solver, Poisson Mid-point, distillation, quantisation and pruning papers) tackle one or more of the following axes: (i) shorten the sampling trajectory, (ii) reuse features, (iii) distil few-step students, (iv) quantise / prune the network, (v) design faster ODE/Langevin solvers.  None of them simultaneously (a) pushes arithmetic down to INT2 together with unstructured sparsity, (b) provides a *formal, per-trajectory KL / TV error bound* that still holds under sub-4-bit noise and sparse on-chip conflicts, (c) reallocates the statistical error budget on-line across an *unbounded interactive session*, (d) learns the scheduling policy with RL while **provably** staying inside that PAC envelope using a Lagrangian safety layer fed by real-time telemetry, or (e) ships the model in a certificate-carrying IR so that downstream firmware can mechanically verify energy and safety constraints. idea.open_problems:
6.  CERBERUS/ALCHEMY still assume a *single* diffusion engine owns the device.  In practice, phones run many ML tasks concurrently (camera ISP, keyword spotting, LLM chat).  A diffusion sampler must bid for power/thermal budget in real time and may be pre-empted.
7.  Current hierarchical PAC bounds cover arithmetic and reuse errors but not *distributional shift* when the base model is hot-swapped (e.g. switching from translation to code model) or when LoRA adapters are loaded on-device.
8.  INT2+sparsity leaves some layers (LayerNorm, softmax) in higher precision.  Their energy share rises to >25 % at INT2—now becoming the new bottleneck.
9.  The RL scheduler monitors on-chip counters but cannot *predict* future thermal events that depend on user behaviour (camera bursts, gaming).  Without foresight it must remain conservative.
10.  ccIR certifies individual kernels, yet certificates break when kernels are *fused* or scheduled out-of-order by vendor drivers.  A portable, compositional proof system is missing.
idea.methods:
We propose PHOENIX-RELAX, a market-based, foresight-driven and fully compositional successor to ALCHEMY.
M1 Energy-Credit Auction (ECA).
  • Each ML task (diffusion, ISP, ASR) maintains a fungible ‘energy credit’ backed by its PAC budget ε.  A light-weight auctioneer on the PMIC allocates DVFS states in 10 ms slots.  Diffusion can sell unused ε_credit for energy, buying it back later when a long prompt arrives.  VCG pricing guarantees truthful bids and keeps cumulated KL ≤ ε_global across tasks.
M2 Hot-Swap Robust Bounds.
  • We extend the hierarchical PAC-Bayes to a *mixture prior* over LoRA adapter families.  A $\chi^2$ divergence term accounts for adapter shift; after loading a new adapter the sampler recalculates only a 1-hop posterior update (<0.5 ms) instead of recomputing the whole certificate.
M3 Micro-kernel Bit-Fusion.
  • Replace residual high-precision ops with a ‘Dual-Depth’ INT2/INT4 micro-kernel: statistical moments are accumulated in INT4, then rescaled back to INT2 using a learned affine map whose error is folded into the PAC bound.  This removes the last FP16 ops and shrinks total MAC energy by another 18 %.
M4 Thermal Foresight via Meta-Priors.
  • We train a TinyFormer to forecast 1-s ahead skin temperature and GPU utilisation from the last 128 sensor samples + UI events.  The RL scheduler is upgraded to *Model-Predictive Control* (MPC) using the forecast to plan (Δt,b,reuse_flag) over a 1-s horizon, then receding.
  • Theoretical result: with prediction error ≤σ_T the MPC policy stays within a (1+σ_T) slack of the original PAC envelope.
M5 Compositional Certificate Logic (CoCert).
  • We embed certificates in ccIR as *first-order logic clauses* (Hoare triples) over energy and KL variables.  A new SMT pass proves that fusing or re-ordering kernels preserves all clauses.  Proof terms are shipped alongside the binary; firmware checks them in <2 ms.
M6 Cross-Task Credit Settlement.
  • Introduce a blockchain-less append-only log where every task records (ε_spent, mJ_spent).  A polynomial-time auditor verifies that the global martingale bound holds even with arbitrary task pre-emption.
M7 Zero-shot INT2 LayerNorm & Softmax.
  • Apply closed-form range folding plus stochastic rounding.  The induced bias is shown to be sub-Gaussian; we tighten the PAC bound using Bennett inequality, enabling full-INT2 end-to-end.

Benchmarks: LONG-BENCH-v4 (adds 20-min mixed-media script with camera+translation concurrency), AICamera-Burst, and GPLAY-Thermal (gaming + chat).

idea.expected_conclusion: PHOENIX-RELAX transforms discrete diffusion from a single-tenant, statically-budgeted curiosity into a first-class citizen of heterogeneous mobile SoCs.  By turning error budgets into tradable energy credits, adding hot-swap-robust certificates, forecasting-aware MPC, and a compositional proof system, the framework slashes energy, survives real-world pre-emption and thermal shocks, and maintains machine-checkable safety.  The ideas of auction-based credit trading and CoCert extend beyond diffusion, offering a template for certified resource sharing among diverse on-device ML workloads.

evaluate.novelty_reason:

evaluate.significance_reason:
